paper_summary: LSU MSc thesis (P. Wehmer, 2008) on the high-strain-rate compressive behaviour of rubber-modified ('hybrid') syntactic foams: DGEBA epoxy (D.E.R. 332 / D.E.H. 24 / GE-8 diluent) filled with 63 vol% 3M Scotchlite glass microspheres (S22, S32, S38 or K46 - same ~40 um outer diameter, different wall thickness) plus 2 vol% ground waste-tyre crumb rubber of 40 or 75 um. Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar tests at 437-1017 /s show peak stress rising with strain rate (strongly for the denser S38/K46 foams, weakly for S22/S32) and compressive modulus rising ~60% from 450 to 1050 /s. Rubber addition lowers modulus relative to plain 65 vol% syntactic foams at low-to-medium rates; 75 um rubber gives ~20% higher peak stress and more than double the modulus of the 40 um rubber foams.

processing.matrix_name: DGEBA epoxy D.E.R. 332 (Dow) + 5 vol% Erisys GE-8 C12-C14 aliphatic glycidyl ether diluent, cured with D.E.H. 24
processing.particle_grade: 3M Scotchlite S22 borosilicate glass microspheres (isostatic crush strength for 80% survival 2.76 MPa, wall 1.26 um)
processing.additional_fillers: 2 vol% ground (crumb) rubber, Rouse Polymerics GF-170, 40 um mean particle size, specific gravity 1.12-1.15; rubber/matrix volume ratio ~5.7%

structure.microstructure_notes: Four-phase hybrid foam: epoxy matrix + 63 vol% glass microspheres + 2 vol% crumb rubber + entrapped-air voids (no degassing applied).

test.standard: Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB / Kolsky bar); no ASTM standard cited
test.specimen_notes: Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (Kolsky bar), maraging steel 18Ni(350) bars; core-drilled cylinder 9.38 mm dia. x 14.0-14.6 mm long, MoS2 grease lubricated interfaces, mild steel pulse shaper (6.73 mm dia. x 3.29 mm). Three duplicate tests per material per strain-rate level. Reported scatter SD=4.8% of the mean modulus.

extraction_notes: All numeric mechanical values in this thesis come from Table 9 (modulus vs strain rate) plus two peak-stress numbers quoted in the text; every peak-stress vs strain-rate data point is plotted only (Figs. 13, 14, 16, 17) with no numbers printed, so no values were read off the plots. data_origin: the twelve Table 9 rows carrying an SD (S22R40/S32R40/S38R40/K46R40 at 437-1017 /s) are the author's own SHPB measurements = primary. The 'Static' rows and the entire right-hand block of Table 9 (plain S22/S32/S38/K46 foams, 65 vol% microspheres, no rubber, including their 703-1688 /s SHPB values) are comparison data whose caption cites refs [10,20,30], so they are marked secondary with the citation kept in sample_label. The two quasi-static peak stresses (S38R40 58 MPa, S38R75 52 MPa) are likewise quoted from ref. [10]. INCONSISTENCY IN THE SOURCE: Table 2 (p. 23) lists quasi-static moduli of 870, 1025, 1300 and 1400 for S22R40, S32R40, S38R40 and K46R40, while Table 9 (p. 45) gives 870, 1025, 2350 and 2550 for the same samples; the Table 9 values were used because Table 9 is the results table. Table 2's modulus column is also headed 'GPa' although the values are clearly MPa (they match Table 9's MPa column); MPa was assumed. Densities from Table 8 (kg/m3 -> g/cm^3) and void volume fractions (% -> fraction, stored as matrix_porosity_fraction) are attached to every hybrid-foam record; the plain foams of the comparison block have no reported density. Microsphere true density, mean diameter (50th percentile), radius ratio and wall thickness are from Table 7. Strain at peak is not tabulated per sample - the text only says peak stress occurs at 1.5-2.0% compressive strain for all foams - so strain_at_failure is null everywhere. Test temperature was set to 25 C (ambient SHPB testing); it is not stated explicitly. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 100 C is the 3 h post-cure (gelled >=36 h at room temperature first); no degassing or pressure was applied during casting. S32R75 has only density/void data in numeric form, so it is recorded once with test_type 'other'.
